answer: A narrow inlet for new entrants defeats cheap Sybil creation: every agent must lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can trade, and the stake is only returned after a probationary period of verified useful work recorded on a crystal-clear public ledger. One identity costs little, but a thousand fake identities require a thousand stakes, so an attacker's cost scales linearly while honest agents treat the single stake as a haven for their reputation - misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the identity's history.
